_doc: M1's motion, rebuilt from scratch on 2026-09-23. Six shots move; eight are held stills. The graph's own motion field carries the same lamp-flame sentence on all fourteen generate shots and animates none of the film's beats, so these are written from the directing pack and the director's action list.
_the_rule_that_decided_it: We do not animate what the model cannot hold. Two things it could not hold: the king's crown, which floated - it stayed at the same height while his head rose under it and changed silhouette across the shot - and lit lamps, whose flames slid along their rims, detached, and in one case were invented outright, a large flame burning in mid-air against the steps with nothing under it. So the crown and the lamps are simply not in any moving shot. Every shot with the king in his crown is a still, and every moving shot is made from a lamp-free frame.
_why_not_patch_it: It was patched, for two rounds: 35 lamps frozen across 13 shots by compositing the approved still back over each one, masked and feathered. It worked - every mask measured 0.000 to 0.49 px of drift - and it was the wrong shape of answer. A patch layer has to be maintained, re-verified on every re-render, and it hid the real question, which is whether a shot should move at all. A held still in a film of held stills is not a defect.
_shape: Every instruction says three things in this order: the beat, what does NOT move, and the ambient life last and smallest. The order is deliberate - the beat first because it is the shot, the negative second because reference-conditioned video will invent a camera move if nobody forbids one, and the ambient last because it is the least important thing in the frame.
standing_rules: Flames stay on their wicks. They may flicker in place; they never slide, drift, detach, multiply or change count.
No new flame, lamp, fire or glowing light appears anywhere in the frame. Nothing burns that is not already burning in the first frame.
The camera does not move. Nothing enters the frame and nothing leaves it. No face, costume, jewellery or ornament changes shape, size or design.
_standing_rules_why: A standing rule is appended to EVERY instruction this film sends, by tools/motion_film.js, rather than pasted into each one by hand - a rule that has to be remembered six times is a rule that will be forgotten once. The flame rules were written after flames slid and then after one was invented from nothing; the third is the director's blanket condition for this rebuild and is a backstop, not a substitute for keeping the crown and the lamps out of the moving shots.

01-02.instruction: The sage walks away from the camera, up the long hall toward the distant dais, seen from behind. An unhurried walk. His draped robe swings and settles with each step and his staff is planted with each second step. The seated ministers on both sides stay completely still and do not turn. Nobody else moves.

01-03.instruction: Seated ministers turn their heads toward the entrance, one after another, unhurried - curiosity, not alarm. Nobody stands, nobody speaks, nobody raises a hand. Their draped cloth settles as they turn. Nothing else in the hall changes.

01-12.instruction: A pair of open hands resting on knees, palms up, completely unchanged. The fingers do not close and do not move. No face is visible. The only movement anywhere is the faintest breath in the draped cloth beneath them.

01-14.instruction: A seated sage's face: the smallest intake of breath, his lips parting slightly, and it stops there. He does not speak. His head does not turn, his seated posture does not change, his beard and hair do not move beyond a single strand settling.

held_as_stills._why: Every one of these has the king in his crown, which the model cannot hold rigid, or a lamp that cannot be removed without remaking the frame. The director's call, 2026-09-23: a held still in a film of held stills is not a defect.
held_as_stills._not_in_either_list: 01-10 appears in neither of the director lists of 2026-09-23 - not among the six to animate, not among the eight to hold. It is held, which is what the rule gives: it is the wide of the ministers with Vasistha and it carries two tall standing lamps and a diya at bottom-right, none of them removed from its still. Flagged rather than decided quietly.
held_as_stills.01-04: the king rises - the crown floated here, twice
held_as_stills.01-05: he comes down the steps - the king in his crown
held_as_stills.01-07: the two men seated - the king in his crown
held_as_stills.01-09: the king again - his crown, and where the model invented a flame in mid-air
held_as_stills.01-10: the wide of the ministers - two standing lamps and a diya, still in the frame
held_as_stills.01-11: the word given - the king in his crown
held_as_stills.01-13: the king at ease - his crown
held_as_stills.01-15: motion_allowed: false in the graph. A reuse of 01-13.
held_as_stills.01-16: motion_allowed: false in the graph. A reuse of 01-14, and the film's final hold.
held_as_stills.01-06: the water at the feet. Animated and then demoted on 2026-09-23: the camera slid 561 px across the shot, the water stopped pouring two thirds of the way through, and two tall gold lamps appeared from nothing at frame-right in the last third - despite the rule against exactly that.
held_as_stills.01-08: the sage waits. Animated and then demoted: the camera slid 13.8 px. It looked fine frame by frame and the measurement caught it, which is the argument for measuring the camera rather than trusting an eye on a slow drift.

_camera_drift._doc: Measured with tools/cameracheck.py - phase correlation of every frame against the first. Every M1 shot is marked `locked` and every instruction says so in words; a generative model drifts the frame anyway, and a slow slide is the hardest defect to see one frame at a time.
_camera_drift._corrected_my_eye_twice: Watching four frames side by side, I read 01-03 as sliding and 01-08 as clean. It is the other way round: 01-03 measures 0.25 px and 01-08 measures 13.84. The eye finds an invented lamp and a stopped stream; the measurement finds a slow drift.
